title: VST images the Lagoon Nebula
caption: The Lagoon Nebula, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: Lagoon Nebula, Messier 8 · constellation Sagittarius · about 5000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This richly detailed view of the Lagoon Nebula, also known as Messier 8, comes from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. The Lagoon is a giant cloud of gas and dust that is busy producing intensely bright young stars, and it is home to young clusters of stars.

Clouds like this are the birthplaces of stars. Where the gas and dust are dense enough, gravity pulls material together until new stars ignite, often in groups that form clusters. The energetic light of those young stars in turn lights up the gas around them.

This picture is only a tiny part of a much bigger project. It comes from one of eleven public surveys of the sky being carried out with ESO telescopes. Together those surveys are building up a vast store of publicly available data that astronomers anywhere in the world can use for their own research.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (58.12 x 39.74 arcminutes) and distance (5000 light years), the frame spans roughly 85 × 58 light-years. Its light set out about 5,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image was taken with ESO's VLT Survey Telescope using u, g, r and i filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter that traces glowing hydrogen. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, and the hydrogen-alpha filter makes the glowing gas much more prominent than it would appear by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: The Lagoon Nebula, a large cloud of glowing gas and dust with young stars.
